wave: CORRECTNESS -- the git VCS integration's shared subprocess-output helper applied a whole-string .trim() that silently stripped git status --porcelain=v1's meaningful leading-space status code, flipping an unstaged change into a falsely-staged one in the repository snapshot's own audit trail
wave_title: Eleventh fix this generation cycle. Following up on a prior survey that flagged runtime/src/inventory/mod.rs and adapter/src/vcs/mod.rs but gave them only brief coverage while its detailed finding was elsewhere, ran a dedicated follow-up survey reading both files in full. inventory/mod.rs turned out to be a thin delegator with no bug-bearing logic of its own; vcs/mod.rs's finding was independently re-verified -- including reproducing the exact git output byte-for-byte against a real git repository -- before any change.
priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity -- highest category in the standing priority order. RepositorySnapshot.status_entries is the literal audit trail backing this project's own EXACT_BASE_SHA_REQUIRED invariant and work-prepare provenance; silently misreporting an unstaged change as staged corrupts that audit trail for the single most common real git state (edited a file, never staged it), not an edge case.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly asked for a full, dedicated read of adapter/src/vcs/mod.rs (previously only briefly touched by an earlier survey). Its finding was independently re-verified before any change: read the real, current git() helper and snapshot_git function directly, then independently reproduced the exact triggering git output against a REAL git repository on this host (git init, an unstaged-only modification, git status --porcelain=v1 | cat -A) to directly observe the literal leading space in real git's own output -- not merely trusting the subagent's description of git's porcelain format.
key_finding: adapter/src/vcs/mod.rs's shared git() helper applied `String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_owned()` to the ENTIRE raw subprocess output before any caller ever splits it into lines. `git status --porcelain=v1` encodes real repository state in a fixed two-column `XY` code at the START of each line, where a literal leading space is semantically meaningful: `" M path"` (index clean, worktree modified -- an UNSTAGED change) is the opposite git state from `"M  path"` (index has the staged modification, worktree clean). Because porcelain entries are emitted in path-sorted order, not grouped by status, whichever entry happens to sort first is exposed to this bug: if its status code begins with a space, the whole-string `.trim()` strips that leading space before `snapshot_git`'s `.lines()` ever sees it, permanently corrupting that one entry's recorded status from unstaged to (falsely) staged. Verified against real git: an unstaged-only file modification produces real stdout `" M file.txt\n"` (confirmed via `cat -A` showing the literal leading space), which the unfixed code recorded as `"M file.txt"` in RepositorySnapshot.status_entries -- exactly backwards.
verification_before_acting: Read the real, current git() helper and snapshot_git function directly in adapter/src/vcs/mod.rs, confirming the exact whole-string .trim() call and that its output feeds status_text before any line-splitting.

Independently reproduced the exact triggering scenario against a REAL git repository on this host (not a mocked/assumed git behavior): git init, a commit, then an unstaged-only file modification, then git status --porcelain=v1 | cat -A -- directly observed the literal leading space (` M file.txt$`) in real git's own output before writing any fix.

Confirmed via directory listing that adapter/src/vcs/ has no existing test file at all, and grepped the workspace for any other reference to status_entries/snapshot_git -- confirmed this parsing path had zero prior test coverage.

Confirmed the report's secondary claim (runtime/src/inventory/mod.rs is a thin delegator with no bug-bearing logic of its own) by independently reading that file -- correctly not treated as a second finding, avoiding a manufactured secondary fix.

design_decisions.question: Fix the shared git() helper, or only the status-specific call site?
design_decisions.decision: Fix the shared git() helper (change .trim() to .trim_end()) rather than adding special-casing at the status call site. This is the narrower, more correct fix: rev-parse HEAD and branch --show-current output never has meaningful leading whitespace (a git SHA/branch name), so trim_end() behaves identically to the old trim() for those callers -- zero behavior change there -- while correctly stopping the leading-space corruption for status --porcelain=v1's output, the one caller where it mattered. A per-call-site special case would have left the shared helper's own contract silently unsafe for any future caller that also needs leading whitespace preserved.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: The shared git() subprocess-output helper no longer strips meaningful leading whitespace from any git command's stdout, closing a real corruption of git status --porcelain=v1's XY status codes in RepositorySnapshot.status_entries for whichever entry happens to sort first when its status begins with a space (the common unstaged-modification case).
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Added an_unstaged_only_modification_keeps_its_leading_space_status_code, the first test this file has ever had: creates a real git repository, commits a file, makes an unstaged-only modification, calls the real snapshot_git against it, and asserts status_entries is exactly [" M file.txt"] (with its real leading space) rather than the corrupted ["M file.txt"]. Falsified per this session's standing discipline: backed up the file, reverted the fix to the original whole-string .trim(), ran the new test, confirmed it failed with the exact expected corruption (left: ["M file.txt"], right: [" M file.txt"]), then restored the fix from backup (git diff --stat and a direct read of the restored file confirmed it exactly matched the fix) and confirmed the test passes.
